description: 3 pages with invented ProQuest-style ebook stamps: a three-line header (a citation that wraps onto a second line, then a "Created from ... on <date>" line) in 8pt at the top of every page, and a copyright line plus an "Ebook pages ... | Printed page N of 3" line at the bottom. All names are invented.
format: Per page: `lines` = expected buildLines(page).map(l => l.text) in reading order; `spoken` = text to speak with DEFAULT_FILTERS; `spokenReadEverything` = text to speak with READ_EVERYTHING; `skipped` = what DEFAULT_FILTERS drop. Spoken text joins lines with single spaces, de-hyphenates "-" + lowercase line starts, and is normalized (ligatures expanded, soft hyphens removed, NBSP/thin space -> space).
notes: DEFAULT_FILTERS (skipHeadersFooters) drops every stamp line, including the wrapped second line of the citation; READ_EVERYTHING speaks them.
Page 2 body text mentions "ProQuest" and "Copyright law" in running prose: it is kept.

lines: Mara Ellison. Tidal Gardens: A Field Guide, Harbor Lane Press, 2019. ProQuest Ebook Central,
http://ebookcentral.proquest.com/lib/lakeview/detail.action?docID=5530481.

Chapter 1
Tidal gardens form where a shallow shelf of rock holds seawater between tides. Small pools
warm quickly in the sun, and their chemistry shifts within a few hours. Animals that live there
must tolerate heat, salt and sudden rain.
Copyright ©2019. Harbor Lane Press. All rights reserved.

Chapter 3
Green algae dominate the high pools, where light is strong and grazers are few. Lower down,
red algae spread beneath the shade of larger brown weeds. Each band of colour marks a
different balance of light and wave action.
Copyright ©2019. Harbor Lane Press. All rights reserved.
